summary.text: Celestial mechanics is the branch of astronomy that studies how objects in outer space move and pull on each other with gravity.
It applies the principles of physics to stars and planets, and its modern analytic form began with Isaac Newton's Principia in 1687.
Two bodies can be predicted with reasonable accuracy, but adding a third creates a problem that cannot be solved exactly, so approximations are used.

facts.label: Name of the field
facts.value: Pierre-Simon Laplace introduced the term celestial mechanics

facts.label: Newton's big idea
facts.value: One set of physical laws describes planets and falling apples

facts.label: Three-body problem
facts.value: It cannot be solved exactly, and Poincaré showed it is not integrable

facts.label: Lagrange points
facts.value: Euler found three equilibrium points, Lagrange two more

facts.label: Mercury's puzzle
facts.value: Its perihelion advanced 43″ per century, beyond known Newtonian perturbations

items.prompt: Astronomers can predict where two bodies pulling on each other will be in the future. A third body joins the system. What changes?

options.label: Newtonian mechanics stops applying, so only general relativity can be used
The three bodies can be treated as one combined mass on a single path
No exact solution exists any longer, so approximate methods are used
The motion becomes impossible to observe, though still exactly computable

items.explain: Adding a third body creates a three-body problem that cannot be solved exactly, and perturbation theory is used to find an approximate solution.

items.prompt: Someone watches a cannon ball fall and the Moon move across the sky. What did Newton's insight say about these motions?

options.label: One set of physical laws can describe both of them
Each follows its own separate set of laws, one for sky and one for ground
Only the falling ball can be described by equations at all
Both are governed by Kepler's elliptical rule alone

items.explain: Newton is credited with the idea that objects in the heavens and objects on the ground obey the same physical laws, unifying celestial and terrestrial dynamics.

items.prompt: Newton called the field "rational mechanics". Over a century later, who gave it the name it has today?

options.label: Gottfried Leibniz, who coined the term dynamics
Henri Poincaré, who wrote two monographs on it
Leonhard Euler, who found equilibrium points
Pierre-Simon Laplace

items.explain: Leibniz brought in the term dynamics, and Laplace introduced the term celestial mechanics over a century after Newton.

items.prompt: A speck of negligible mass is placed at one of the three equilibrium points Euler found along a line through two large masses. What happens?

options.label: It is pulled toward the larger mass and falls into it
It stays there in a stable orbit
It is thrown out of the system at once
It loops tightly around the smaller mass

items.explain: Euler showed three equilibrium points lie on a straight line through the two primary masses, and a body of infinitesimal mass there would remain in a stable orbit.

items.prompt: Before Kepler, predicting where planets appear and explaining why they move were largely separate efforts. What did Kepler change?

options.label: He showed that predicting positions was pointless and only causes mattered
He derived the planetary orbits from Newton's law of gravitation
He joined predictive geometrical astronomy with physical concepts
He dropped geometry and used only numerical tables

items.explain: Kepler closely integrated predictive geometrical astronomy with physical concepts in his 1609 New Astronomy, before Newton's gravitation law existed.

items.prompt: Astronomers in different countries disagreed over positions and constants. How was the confusion resolved?

options.label: Each country kept its own constants and published conversion tables
One observatory was made responsible for all observations
Tables were dropped in favour of computing positions fresh each night
Everyone adopted one astronomer's recalculated constants as the shared standard

items.explain: Newcomb recalculated the major astronomical constants, and international conferences agreed that ephemerides should be based on his calculations.
